title: How to Read a Map
summary: Directions, scale, legends and grid lines: the four tools that unlock any map.

steps.title: Directions
sentences: The four main directions are north, east, south and west.
Between them are north-east, south-east, south-west and north-west.
A compass has a magnetic needle that points north, and many maps have a small compass rose to show directions.

steps.title: Scale
sentences: A map is a small picture of a big place.
The scale tells how much smaller it is, for example 1 centimetre on the map stands for 10 kilometres on the ground.
Use a ruler and the scale to find real distances.
points: Scale links map to the ground

steps.title: Legend
sentences: A map uses signs and colours instead of words.
The legend or key explains them: blue for water, green for forests and a small symbol for a railway or a temple.

steps.title: Latitude and longitude
sentences: Imaginary lines called latitudes run east to west, and longitudes run north to south.
The equator is the 0 degree latitude line.
Every place on Earth can be named by its latitude and longitude, like an address for the whole planet.

facts: The Prime Meridian, the 0 degree longitude line, passes through Greenwich in London.
Chennai is at about 13 degrees north and 80 degrees east.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through India.

quiz.q: What does a map's legend show?
quiz.why: The legend explains the signs and colours.

quiz.q: Which line is at 0 degrees latitude?
What does a map scale tell you?
options: How much smaller the map is than the real place
quiz.why: It tells how distances on the map compare with real distances.
